subject: Copywriting
title: Confirmation Bias in Copy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Confirmation Bias in Copy.

hook.text: People seek information that confirms what they already believe. Smart copy doesn't fight beliefs—it mirrors them.

buildup.text: A vegan doesn't need convincing that plant milk is good. Copy that confirms their choice builds fierce loyalty.

discovery.text: Political ads target existing supporters, not opponents. Copy works best when it says what people want to hear.

twist.text: Confirmation bias means facts rarely change minds. The best copy aligns with identity, then gently redirects.

climax.text: Apple's 'Think Different' didn't convince new users. It made existing fans feel smarter for buying Apple.

punchline.text: Don't change minds. Confirm them. That's how copy sells.

quiz.question: How does effective copy use confirmation bias?
options: It confirms what readers already believe
